subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which statement best defines diffusion?
options: The net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration, down a concentration gradient, from their random movement
The movement of water molecules across a partially permeable membrane
The movement of particles from a lower to a higher concentration using energy
The bulk flow of liquid through a tube caused by a pressure difference
questions.explain: Diffusion is the net movement of particles down a concentration gradient resulting from their random motion.

questions.q: Does diffusion require energy from respiration?
options: No, it is a passive process
Yes, it always requires energy from respiration
Yes, but only in animal cells
Yes, but only against a concentration gradient
questions.explain: Diffusion is passive and does not use energy from respiration because particles move down the gradient.

questions.q: Which change would increase the rate of diffusion across a surface?
options: Increasing the surface area over which diffusion occurs
Decreasing the temperature of the system
Reducing the concentration gradient
Increasing the distance the particles must travel
questions.explain: A larger surface area allows more particles to diffuse at once, raising the rate.

questions.q: A drop of blue dye is placed in a beaker of warm water and another identical drop in cold water. Which observation is expected?
options: The dye spreads faster in the warm water
The dye spreads faster in the cold water
The dye spreads at the same rate in both
The dye does not spread in either beaker
questions.explain: Higher temperature gives particles more kinetic energy, so they move and diffuse faster.

questions.q: Which substance is absorbed into the blood in the alveoli of the lungs mainly by diffusion?
options: Oxygen
Glucose against a gradient
Mineral ions into root hairs
Large protein molecules
questions.explain: Oxygen diffuses from the alveolar air, where it is in higher concentration, into the blood.

questions.q: Why does raising the temperature increase the rate of diffusion?
options: Particles gain more kinetic energy and move faster
The concentration gradient is reversed
The membrane becomes impermeable
Energy from respiration is released into the particles
questions.explain: Warmer particles have greater kinetic energy, so they move and mix more rapidly.

questions.q: Which statement best defines osmosis?
options: The net movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential to a region of lower water potential, through a partially permeable membrane
The movement of any particle down a concentration gradient
The movement of mineral ions into a cell using energy
The evaporation of water from a leaf surface
questions.explain: Osmosis is the net movement of water across a partially permeable membrane down a water potential gradient.

questions.q: Osmosis takes place across which type of membrane?
options: A partially permeable membrane
A fully impermeable membrane
A membrane that only allows solutes through
A rigid cellulose cell wall only
questions.explain: A partially permeable membrane lets water molecules pass but restricts larger solute particles.

questions.q: A plant cell is placed in pure water. What happens to the cell?
options: It takes in water by osmosis and becomes turgid
It loses water by osmosis and becomes plasmolysed
It bursts because it has no cell wall
Nothing changes because the wall stops all water
questions.explain: Water enters the cell down the water potential gradient and the wall resists expansion, making it turgid.

questions.q: A plant cell is placed in a concentrated sugar solution. Which change occurs?
options: Water leaves the cell and the membrane pulls away from the wall (plasmolysis)
Water enters the cell and it becomes turgid
The cell bursts
The cell wall dissolves
questions.explain: The external solution has lower water potential, so water leaves and the cell plasmolyses.

questions.q: Pieces of potato are left in salt solution and their mass decreases. What does this indicate?
options: Water moved out of the potato cells by osmosis
Water moved into the potato cells by osmosis
Salt moved into the cells by diffusion only
Active transport moved water out of the cells
questions.explain: A mass decrease shows the cells lost water to the more concentrated (lower water potential) salt solution.

questions.q: An animal cell such as a red blood cell placed in pure water will:
options: Swell and burst because it has no cell wall
Become turgid and firm
Plasmolyse
Remain unchanged
questions.explain: Without a cell wall to resist it, the cell takes in water and bursts.

questions.q: Water always moves by osmosis towards the solution with:
options: The lower water potential
The higher water potential
The larger volume
The higher temperature
questions.explain: Net water movement is from higher to lower water potential across a partially permeable membrane.

questions.q: A wilting plant has soft, drooping leaves. In terms of cells, this is because the cells have:
options: Lost water and become flaccid
Gained water and become turgid
Undergone active transport of ions
Increased their water potential
questions.explain: Cells that lose water become flaccid, so they no longer support the leaf and it wilts.

questions.q: Which statement best defines active transport?
options: The movement of particles through a cell membrane from a lower to a higher concentration, using energy from respiration
The net movement of particles down a concentration gradient
The movement of water across a partially permeable membrane
The random movement of particles until evenly spread
questions.explain: Active transport moves particles against the concentration gradient using energy from respiration.

questions.q: Where does the energy for active transport come from?
options: Respiration
Diffusion
Evaporation
Osmosis
questions.explain: Active transport requires energy released by respiration to pump particles against the gradient.

questions.q: How does active transport differ from diffusion?
options: Active transport moves particles against the concentration gradient and needs energy
Active transport only moves water molecules
Active transport always moves particles down the gradient
Active transport does not involve the cell membrane
questions.explain: Unlike diffusion, active transport works against the gradient and requires energy from respiration.

questions.q: Which is an example of active transport in a plant?
options: Uptake of mineral ions by root hair cells
Loss of water vapour from leaves
Movement of oxygen into leaf cells by diffusion
Water entering root cells by osmosis
questions.explain: Root hair cells absorb ions from soil against the gradient by active transport.

questions.q: What is the role of protein carrier molecules in active transport?
options: They bind particles and move them across the membrane using energy
They break down the cell membrane
They allow water to pass through freely
They store energy from the sun
questions.explain: Carrier proteins in the membrane transport specific particles against the gradient using energy.

questions.q: A cell absorbs glucose from the gut even when the glucose concentration inside the cell is already higher than outside. Which process is responsible?
options: Active transport
Diffusion
Osmosis
Evaporation
questions.explain: Absorbing glucose against its concentration gradient requires active transport using energy.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610) syllabus; Movement Into & Out of Cells
